questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

You are the __beautiful__ woman I have ever seen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **most beautiful.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the correct superlative form of the adjective should be used.
 
• The term **'beautiful'** is an **adjective** that can be modified to its **superlative **form for comparison.
 
• The presence of **'the' **before 'beautiful' hints at the fact that the** superlative form **of **'beautiful' **should be used.
 
• The correct superlative form of **'beautiful'** is **'most beautiful'**, indicating that no other woman is more beautiful than the one being referred to.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *You are the most beautiful woman I have ever seen*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In English grammar, adjectives have three degrees of comparison: positive, comparative, and superlative.
 
 
• **Positive degree:** describes a single item/person (e.g., beautiful).
 
• **Comparative degree:** compares two items/people (e.g., more beautiful).
 
• **Superlative degree:** compares more than two items/people (e.g., most beautiful).
